findings.summary: Weekly discovery re-sync (sync-supabase-nv.js) unconditionally recomputed package_status from ngem.json's document-discovery list on every run, silently resetting PACKAGE_COMPLETE/PACKAGE_PARTIAL rows back to PACKAGE_DISCOVERED/NOT_STARTED and undoing real acquisition work.
findings.fix: Sync now checks state_contract_opportunities + apie_contract_processing for any id already at COMPLETE/PARTIAL and omits package_status/package_document_count/package_completed_at from that row's upsert payload entirely, relying on PostgREST merge-duplicates leaving omitted columns untouched.

apps.role: Canonical lifecycle tables (state_contract_opportunities, apie_contract_processing, apie_contract_archive), promotion/archive logic, requirements-extraction worker

findings.summary: requirements_extraction_status stays NOT_STARTED indefinitely for NV/NGEM-sourced records. The shared extraction worker (contract-package-engine.js / command-contract-package-worker-background.js) exists and runs on schedule, but is currently built only against California sources (CalEProcure, CivicPlus). NGEM/NV was never integrated into it, so even a record that reaches state_contract_opportunities with PACKAGE_COMPLETE stays match_readiness_status=BLOCKED_REQUIREMENTS_INCOMPLETE indefinitely -- it will never surface as a real dashboard match without this.
findings.recommendation: This is the real remaining blocker to a substantial, matchable NV contract volume. Scope as its own focused build: extend the shared requirements-extraction worker to accept NGEM's raw payload shape, or write an NGEM-specific extraction path that writes to the same requirements/requirements_extraction_status columns.

apps.role: Public-facing dashboard, matching UI, resident-state capture during business intake

findings.summary: Live tested with Apropos Group LLC's own real site (address: North Las Vegas, Nevada 89081). The AI website-discovery model (gpt-5-mini, reasoning effort low) returned resident_state="NE" instead of "NV" despite the literal state name appearing on the page. resident_state feeds the dashboard's Resident State matching filter directly, so a wrong derivation silently breaks geographic matching for the affected business with no visible error.
findings.fix: Tightened the discovery prompt to require the literal state name on the page be mapped to its standard USPS abbreviation rather than inferred from the city, and to withhold resident_state entirely when not confident. Does not eliminate all future LLM derivation errors (inherently probabilistic) but directly targets the reproduced failure mode.
